messages.subject: Re: xlsx speed
parts:
Hi Scott, 

No changes were made to slow things down intentionally.  I certainly don't notice it with my setup.  I've sent your question to the list, in case somebody else has encountered the same problem. 

Try different versions/OS just to make sure you can clearly isolate the issue. 

Adrian


On Mon, Jun 3, 2013 at 11:04 AM, Ray, Scott (SL) <sl...@dow.com> wrote:
Hello – I’ve been using the xlsx R package successfully on a Windows 7 (32 bit) computer for several months.  Your package has been very useful.  However, I recently upgraded from R 2.15.2 to R 2.15.3 (I updated and/or reinstalled all packages) and now xlsx functions run very slowly, if at all.  Both read.xlsx and write.xlsx are affected.  Smaller tables (~100 rows X ~8 columns) now take 5 minutes or more to write.  Larger tables (~1000 rows x 10 columns) fail with a Java heap space error message.  In comparison, these same operations took only a few seconds (max) under R 2.15.2.  Switching to read.xlsx2 and write.xlsx2 does not help.  Do you have any advice?  Scott

messages.author: 39408223a5f9f8a8
messages.subject: Re: xlsx speed
parts:
Are you sure that the newer version is the only thing that has
changed? Is it possible that your template has changed too? It could
be something dumb like you changed the format of a whole row or a
column; now, instead of reading a few non-empty cells, R has to read a
whole column which can take a very long time. (theory not tested.)
